decision.summaryForCoordinator: No blockers, no SHOULD-FIX, with the same caveat I attached to G26 v1. Everything asserted verifies: 3/3 cited digests - including harness.DR-G19 v1 at 5ada112a, a digest I independently pinned earlier this session, so that cross-reference checks from both directions; all five carried cells character-exact; the three-member semicolon split derived and rejoined exactly, all three members carrying exactByteIntent and passProperty; D-153 accurate clause by clause. Two things are handled well. First, EV-1 specifies its member as retaining the ABSENCE of a sealed-Run label rather than comparing against a minted positive class - the right way to specify this gate without minting the thing it forbids. Second, the G19 boundary is now symmetric: this file refuses to take over G19, and the G19 v1 file I accepted earlier refuses to take over G27, with neither claiming the overlap. The right NT-6 is pinned twice; DR-133's NT-6 is a genuinely different live class (d9-exit-hosttermination-refused, riding G21), so that check mattered. The caveat: at 5315 bytes this is the second consecutive subject roughly a seventh the size of the fuller harness specs, missing the same eighteen sibling-common keys - whatThisCloses, failsIf, a corpus block, a platforms block, a top-level passProperty among them - plus measures on every member. I probed the three places the thinness could hide a defect (purpose promising corpus intent stated only distributively; the bare 'NT-6'; the live 'pass all' bound to no enumerated domain) and none is false against live bytes or admits a wrong pass, so I charge none. With two in a row, the coordinator may want to settle deliberately whether the preview-gate specs are held to the fuller form. 20 attacks run, 20 refuted.
